questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.4\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force $F(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\,\text{N}$ is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.4{y}^{″}=-ky+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+\frac{5k}{2}y=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=\frac{5k}{2}\,⟹\,k=\frac{2}{5}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t),$ which is $5,$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{2}{5}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{2}{5}\cdot {5}^{2}=10\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

$$
F(t)=(3{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)-\frac{3}{2})\,\text{N}
$$

is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.5{y}^{″}=-ky+(3{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)-\frac{3}{2}).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+2ky=3(2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)-1).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=2k\,⟹\,k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=3(2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)-1)$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$ Since

$$
f(t)=3(2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)-1)=3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),
$$

the frequency of the external periodic force is $4.$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {4}^{2}=8\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $4.$ Therefore,
$\omega =4.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =4$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[16(D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-16(C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)]+16t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ 16D\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-16C\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=0$ and $D=\frac{5}{8}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+\frac{5}{8}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Only solution II matches the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)-t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $3.$ Therefore,
$\omega =3.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =3$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(6D-9Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-(6C+9Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)]+9t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)) & =-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) \\ 6D\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-6C\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t) & =-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+6\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=-1$ and $D=-\frac{1}{2}.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t+ϕ)-t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t+ϕ)-t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)-t\operatorname{cos}⁡(3t)-\frac{1}{2}t\operatorname{sin}⁡(3t)$

Only solution III matches the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
